11.h: 7 - Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr * ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf al-Badrī
11.t:
Ibn ʿAbd al-Dār ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb, the chief, the martyr, the foremost (3) , Badrī (البدري), al-Qurashī, al-ʿAbdarī.
Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib said: The first of the Emigrants to come to us was Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr.
We said to him: What has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ done?
He said: He is where he is, and his companions are following in my footsteps. Then ⟦1:145⟧
ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm, of Banū Fihr, the blind man, came to us after him ... , and he mentioned the hadith (1) .
الأعمش: عن أبي وائل، عن خباب، قال:
We emigrated with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking the face of Allah, so our reward fell upon Allah. Among us were those who passed on to their destiny without eating anything of their reward, among them Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, who was killed on the day of Uḥud and left nothing but a striped cloak: when we covered his head, his feet showed, and when we covered his feet, his head showed.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Cover his head, and put some idhkhir over his feet) .
And among us are those whose fruit has ripened, and he is gathering it (2) .
شعبة: عن سعد بن إبراهيم: سمع أباه يقول:
Food was brought to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and he began to weep, and said:
Ḥamzah was killed, and nothing was found to shroud him in except a garment ⟦1:146⟧ only, and Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr was killed, and nothing was found to shroud him in except a garment only. I fear that our good things have been hastened for us in our worldly life. And he kept weeping (1) .
ابن إسحاق: حدثني يزيد بن زياد، عن القرظي (2) ، عمن سمع علي بن أبي طالب يقول:
That he drew water for a Jew's orchard in return for a palmful of dates.
He said: I came to the mosque, and Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr appeared before us in a cloak of his patched with sheepskin, and he had been the most pampered and most delicate youth in Mecca. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he remembered the luxury he had been in and saw the state he was now in, and his eyes overflowed for him, then he said: (Are you better today, or when one of you is served in the morning a platter of bread and meat?) .
We said: On that day we would be better: we would be spared the burden and free ourselves for worship.
He said: (Rather, you are better today than you would be on that day) (3) . ⟦1:147⟧
ابن إسحاق: حدثني صالح بن كيسان، عن سعد بن مالك، قال:
Before the Hijrah we suffered the harshness and hardship of life and could not endure it. Then no sooner had we emigrated than hunger and hardship befell us, and we grew strong through them and became powerful against them.
As for Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, he was the most pampered youth in Mecca between his parents, as far as we knew. When what befell us befell him, he could not bear it. I saw him with his skin peeling off him as a snake's skin peels, and I saw him collapse so that he could not walk, so we would hold bows out to him and then carry him on our shoulders.
And I saw myself once, I got up to urinate at night, and I heard beneath my urine something pushing against it; I felt it with my hand, and it was a piece of camel hide. I took it, washed it until I had softened it, then burned it with fire, then pounded it, split it into three pieces, and fortified myself with it for three days (1) .
Ibn Isḥāq said: Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr fought in defence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he was killed.
Ibn Qamiʾah al-Laythī killed him, thinking he was the Messenger of Allah, and went back to Quraysh and said: I have killed Muḥammad.
When Muṣʿab was killed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the banner to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and to men from among the Muslims (2) . ⟦1:148⟧

12.h: 8 - Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad ibn Hilāl * (ت، ق)
12.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm ibn Yaqaẓah ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb.
The great chief, the foster brother of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the son of his paternal aunt: Barrah bint ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
One of the first foremost, he emigrated to Abyssinia, then emigrated to Medina, witnessed Badr, and died some months after it, and he had children (1) who were Companions (الصحابي), such as ʿUmar, Zaynab and others.
When the waiting period of his wife Umm Salamah ended, the Prophet ﷺ married her.
She narrated from her husband Abū Salamah the saying at the time of calamity, and she used to say: Who is better than Abū Salamah? She did not think that Allah would replace him for her in her calamity with his like; then, when the master of mankind was opened to her, she rejoiced with the greatest rejoicing. ⟦1:150⟧
He died in middle age, in the year 3 of the Hijrah (may Allah be pleased with him).
Ibn Isḥāq said: He was the first to emigrate to Abyssinia, then he came back with ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn when the latter came back from Abyssinia, and Abū Ṭālib gave him protection.
I say: They returned when they heard of the conversion of the people of Mecca, at the revelation of Sūrat al-Najm.
Muṣʿab ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: Umm Salamah bore him in Abyssinia: Salamah, ʿUmar, Durrah and Zaynab.
I say: These were born in Abyssinia only before the year of the Hijrah.
الأعمش: عن شقيق، عن أم سلمة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (When you attend the dying, speak good, for the angels say amen to what you say) .
She said: When Abū Salamah died, I said:
O Messenger of Allah! What should I say?
He said: (Say: O Allah, forgive him, and grant us after him a good outcome) .
And Allah gave me after him one better than him: the Messenger of Allah (1) ﷺ.
حماد بن سلمة: أنبأنا ثابت، عن عمر بن أبي سلمة، عن أم سلمة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (When a calamity befalls one of you, let him say: Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him ⟦1:151⟧ we return; O Allah, with You I seek reward for my calamity, so reward me in it and give me in exchange something better than it) .
When Abū Salamah was dying, I said that, and I wanted to say: and give me in exchange something better than it, but I said: And who is better than Abū Salamah?
I did not cease until I said it. When her waiting period ended, Abū Bakr proposed to her and she refused him, and ʿUmar proposed to her and she refused him, and the Prophet ﷺ sent word to her.
She said: Welcome to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to his messenger (1) , and he mentioned the hadith (2) . ⟦1:152⟧
Al-Wāqidī said: حدثنا عمر بن عثمان (1) اليربوعي، عن سلمة بن عبد الله بن (2) عمر بن أبي سلمة وغيره، they said:
Abū Salamah witnessed Uḥud, and he was staying at al-ʿĀliyah among Banū Umayyah ibn Zayd; he was wounded at Uḥud and stayed a month treating his wound.
When the new moon of Muḥarram appeared, the Prophet ﷺ called him and said: (Go out on this expedition) .
He tied a banner for him and said: (March until you reach the land of Banū Asad, and raid (3) them) .
He had with him one hundred and fifty men, and they marched until they reached the nearest (4) Qaṭan of their waters, and seized their grazing livestock; then he returned to Medina after some ten-odd nights (5) .
ʿUmar ibn ʿUthmān said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUbayd narrated to me, saying:
When Abū Salamah entered Medina his wound reopened, and he died with three nights remaining of (6) Jumādā al-Ākhirah, meaning: in the year 4.
It is said: Abū Salamah died in the year 3.

13.h: 9 - ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn ibn Ḥabīb ibn Wahb al-Jumaḥī *
13.t:
Ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Jumaḥ ibn ʿAmr ibn Huṣayṣ ibn Kaʿb al-Jumaḥī, Abū al-Sāʾib. ⟦1:153⟧
One of the leaders of the Emigrants and of the pious friends of Allah, those who were successful in dying during the lifetime of their Prophet, who prayed over them.
Abū al-Sāʾib (may Allah be pleased with him) was the first to be buried in al-Baqīʿ (1) .
Kathīr ibn Zayd al-Madanī narrated from al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said:
When the Prophet ﷺ buried ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, he said to a man: (Bring that rock and put it at the grave of my brother, so that I may know it by it, and so that I may bury beside him those of my family whom I bury) .
The man got up but could not lift it, and he - meaning the one who narrated to him - said:
It is as though I am looking at the whiteness of the forearms of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he carried it until he set it down at his grave (2) .
This is mursal (مرسل).
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: I heard Saʿd say:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned down tabattul from ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn (3) , and had he permitted (4) him, we would have castrated ourselves (5) . ⟦1:154⟧
Abū ʿUmar al-Namarī said: Abū al-Sāʾib accepted Islam after thirteen men, made both Hijrahs, and died after Badr; he was a devout worshipper (العابد) (1) , diligent, and he, ʿAlī and Abū Dharr intended to castrate themselves (2) .
It is narrated from the mursal (مرسل) narrations of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, who said:
The first to be buried at Baqīʿ al-Gharqad was ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed a stone at his head and said: (This is the grave of our predecessor (3)) .
He was one of those who forbade wine in the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية).
ابن المبارك: عن عمر بن سعيد، عن ابن سابط:
ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn said: I will not drink a drink that takes away my reason, makes those lower than me laugh at me, and drives me to give my noble daughter in marriage.
When wine was prohibited, he said: Woe to it, my sight had been piercing in it (4) .
This is a disconnected report that is not established; wine was only prohibited after his death (5) . ⟦1:155⟧
سفيان بن وكيع: حدثنا ابن وهب، عن عمرو بن الحارث، حدثني أبو النضر، عن زياد، عن ابن عباس:
That the Prophet ﷺ entered upon ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn when he died and bent over him; then he raised his head, and they seemed to see the trace of weeping.
Then he knelt a second time, then raised his head, and they saw him weeping.
Then he knelt a third time and raised his head with sobbing, so they knew that he was weeping, and the people wept.
He said: (Stop; this is from Satan) .
Then he said: (I seek forgiveness of Allah. O Abū al-Sāʾib! You have left it without being tainted by anything of it (1)) .
حماد بن سلمة: عن علي بن زيد، عن يوسف بن مهران، عن ابن عباس، قال:
When Ibn Maẓʿūn died, his wife said: Blessed are you with Paradise.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at her with a look of anger and said: (What makes you know?) .
She said: Your horseman and your companion.
He said: (I am the Messenger of Allah, and I do not know what will be done with me or with him) .
The people felt apprehensive for ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, and the women wept, and ʿUmar began to quiet them.
He said: (Gently, O ʿUmar!) . Then he said: ⟦1:156⟧
(Beware of the wailing of Satan. Whatever comes from the eye is from Allah and from mercy, and whatever comes from the hand and the tongue is from Satan (1)) .
يعلى بن عبيد: حدثنا الإفريقي، عن سعد بن مسعود، that ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn said:
O Messenger of Allah! I do not like my wife to see my nakedness.
He said: (Why?) .
He said: I am shy of that.
He said: (Allah has made her a garment for you, and made you a garment for her) .
This is disconnected (2) .
Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated from al-Zuhrī:
That ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn wanted to castrate himself and wander the earth.
The Prophet ﷺ said to him: (Do you not have in me a good example? He is not of my community who castrates or is castrated (3)) .
Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī narrated from Abū Burdah:
The wife of ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn visited the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and they saw her in a poor state.
They said to her: What is the matter with you? There is no one in Quraysh richer than your husband!
She said: As for his night, he is standing in prayer, and as for his day, he is fasting.
The Prophet ﷺ met him and said: (Do you not ⟦1:157⟧
have in me an example ... ) the hadith (1) .
He said: After that she came to them perfumed as if she were a bride.
حماد بن زيد: حدثنا معاوية بن عياش، عن أبي قلابة:
That ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn sat devoting himself to worship, and the Prophet ﷺ came to him and said: (O ʿUthmān! Allah did not send me with monasticism, and the best religion with Allah is the tolerant Ḥanīfiyyah (2)) .
From ʿĀʾishah bint Qudāmah, who said:
ʿUthmān, Qudāmah and ʿAbd Allāh, the sons of Maẓʿūn, and Maʿmar ibn al-Ḥārith - when they emigrated - stayed with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah al-ʿAjlānī.
Al-Wāqidī said: The family of Maẓʿūn were among those who left en masse for the Hijrah, and their houses in Mecca were locked (3) .
And from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ marked out for the family of Maẓʿūn the site of their house today in Medina (4) . ⟦1:158⟧
He died: in Shaʿbān, in the year 3.
الثوري: عن عاصم بن عبيد الله (1) ، عن القاسم بن محمد، عن عائشة:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kissed ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn while he was dead, and his tears were flowing on the cheek of ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn (2) .
Al-Tirmidhī graded it authentic (الصحيح).
Mālik narrated from Abū al-Naḍr, who said:
When the funeral of ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn passed by, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (You have gone and have not been tainted by anything of it (3)) .
إبراهيم بن سعد: عن ابن شهاب، عن خارجة بن زيد، عن أم العلاء، one of the women who gave the pledge, and she mentioned:
That ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn fell ill among them, and we nursed him until he died.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and I said: My testimony for you, Abū al-Sāʾib, is that Allah has honoured you!
The Messenger of Allah said: (What makes you know?) .
I said: I do not know, may my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, then who?
He said: (As for him, certainty has come to him, and by Allah I hope good for him, and I am the Messenger of Allah, yet I do not know what will be done with me) .
She said: By Allah, I will never vouch for anyone after him.
She said: It grieved me ⟦1:159⟧ that, and I slept, and I saw a flowing spring belonging to ʿUthmān.
I told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he said: (That is his deed (1)) .
حماد بن سلمة: حدثنا علي بن زيد، عن يوسف بن مهران، عن ابن عباس بنحوه، and he added:
When the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, he said: (Join (2) our good predecessor, ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn (3)) .
الواقدي: حدثنا معمر، عن الزهري، عن عبيد الله:
That ʿUmar said: When ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn died without having been killed, he fell in my esteem, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died.
I said: Woe to you, our best are dying; then Abū Bakr died.
He said: ʿUthmān returned in my esteem to his station (4) .
And from ʿĀʾishah bint Qudāmah, who said:
The sons of Maẓʿūn closely resembled one another; ʿUthmān was very dark-skinned, with a large beard (may Allah be pleased with him) (5) . ⟦1:160⟧

14.h: 10 - Qudāmah ibn Maẓʿūn Abū ʿAmr al-Jumaḥī *
14.t:
One of the first foremost Badrīs (البدري), he was governor of Bahrain for ʿUmar, and was one of the maternal uncles of the Mother of the Believers Ḥafṣah and of Ibn ʿUmar, and the husband of her paternal aunt Ṣafiyyah bint al-Khaṭṭāb, one of the female Emigrants.
Qudāmah made the Hijrah to Abyssinia, and once he drank wine by interpretation, taking as evidence the saying of Allah the Exalted: “There is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten” , the verse [Qurʾān 5:93]; so ʿUmar applied the fixed penalties (الحدود) to him and dismissed him from Bahrain (1) . ⟦1:161⟧
Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī said: No Badrī (البدري) was given the fixed penalties (الحدود) for wine other than him (1) .
I say: Rather, there was also Nuʿaymān ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī al-Najjārī, the man of jesting (2) .
Ibn Saʿd said:
Qudāmah had these children: ʿUmar, Fāṭimah and ʿĀʾishah; he made the second Hijrah to Abyssinia, and witnessed Badr and Uḥud (3) .
And from ʿĀʾishah bint Qudāmah: that her father died in the year 36, aged 68, and he did not dye his grey hair, and he was tall and dark (may Allah be pleased with him) (4) . ⟦1:162⟧

15.h: 11 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maẓʿūn al-Jumaḥī Abū Muḥammad *
15.t:
One of the first foremost, he witnessed Badr together with his brothers: ʿUthmān, Qudāmah, and al-Sāʾib, his brother's son, and ʿAbd Allāh made the second Hijrah to Abyssinia (1) .
Ibn Saʿd said: He witnessed Badr, Uḥud and the Trench, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with Sahl ibn ʿUbayd ibn al-Muʿallā al-Anṣārī.
He said: And he died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUthmān in the year 30, aged 60 (2) .

16.h: 12 - al-Sāʾib ibn ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn al-Jumaḥī **
16.t:
His mother: Khawlah bint Ḥakīm al-Sulamiyyah.
And her mother: Ḍaʿīfah bint al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams.
He emigrated to Abyssinia and was one of the renowned archers, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with Ḥārithah ibn Surāqah al-Anṣārī, who was killed at Badr and who attained al-Firdaws (3) . ⟦1:163⟧
Ibn Saʿd said (1) : Al-Sāʾib ibn ʿUthmān witnessed Badr according to the report of Ibn Isḥāq, Abū Maʿshar and al-Wāqidī.
Ibn ʿUqbah did not mention him.
Hishām ibn al-Kalbī used to say: The one who witnessed it was al-Sāʾib ibn Maẓʿūn, the full brother of ʿUthmān.
Ibn Saʿd said (2) : This is an error.
Until he said: An arrow struck him on the day of al-Yamāmah in the year 12.
He said: And he died of it.

17.h: 13 - Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah al-Qurashī al-ʿAbshamī *
17.t:
The great chief, the martyr, Abū Ḥudhayfah, son of the shaykh of the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية): ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb al-Qurashī, al-ʿAbshamī, Badrī (البدري). ⟦1:164⟧
One of the first foremost, and his name was Muhashshim (1) - so it is said -.
He accepted Islam before they entered the House of al-Arqam.
He emigrated to Abyssinia twice, and Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah was born to him there, that rebel (2) against ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān; Sahlah bint Suhayl ibn ʿAmr bore him to him, she being the woman with prolonged bleeding (3) .
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf married her, and she is the one who nursed Sālim when he was grown, so that he might have access to her, and the two were singled out for that ruling according to the majority of scholars (4) .
And from Abū al-Zinād: that Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn ʿUtbah called his father to single combat on the day of Badr.
His sister Umm Muʿāwiyah, Hind bint ʿUtbah, said: ⟦1:165⟧
The cross-eyed, the one with the superfluous tooth, whose omen is blameworthy ... Abū Ḥudhayfah is the worst of people in religion
Did you not thank him who raised you from childhood ... until you grew into a young man without crookedness (1)
He said: Abū Ḥudhayfah was tall, handsome of face, with teeth set one behind another, and he is the one with the superfluous tooth.
Abū Ḥudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him) was martyred on the day of al-Yamāmah, in the year 12, he and his client (المولى) Sālim.
His brother Abū Hāshim ibn ʿUtbah accepted Islam late; he accepted Islam on the day of the Conquest, and his Islam was good, and he fought in jihad and settled in Syria, and was righteous and religious.
He has a report from the Prophet ﷺ in (al-Tirmidhī), (al-Nasāʾī) and (Ibn Mājah).
He died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUthmān, and he is the brother of the martyr Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr through his mother, and the maternal uncle of the caliph Muʿāwiyah.
روى منصور بن المعتمر، عن أبي وائل، حدثنا سمرة بن سهم، قال:
I came to Abū Hāshim ibn ʿUtbah when he was stricken with plague, and Muʿāwiyah entered to visit him, and he wept.
He said: What makes you weep, uncle? Is it pain or eagerness for the world?
He said: No, neither; but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a covenant with me that I have not kept.
He said to me: (O Abū Hāshim! Perhaps you will live to see wealth divided among people; all that suffices you from gathering the world is a servant and a mount in the way of Allah) .
And I have found it, and I have amassed (2) . ⟦1:166⟧
In a mursal (مرسل) narration: Would that it were old dry dung!
It is said: Abū Ḥudhayfah lived 53 years.

18.t:
One of the first foremost, the Badrīs (البدري), those brought near, the knowledgeable.
Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah said: He is Sālim ibn Maʿqil, originally (1) from Iṣṭakhr; he allied himself with Abū Ḥudhayfah, but the one who freed him was Thubaytah bint Yiʿār al-Anṣāriyyah, the wife of Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn ʿUtbah, and Abū Ḥudhayfah adopted him; so he said.
Ibn Abī Mulaykah narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad:
That Sahlah bint Suhayl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, she being the wife of Abū Ḥudhayfah, and said:
O Messenger of Allah! Sālim is with me, and he has reached what men reach.
He said: (Nurse him, and when you have nursed him, what is forbidden to you from a mahram becomes forbidden) .
Umm Salamah said: The wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ refused that anyone should enter upon them by means of this nursing, and they said:
It was only a special concession for Sālim (2) . ⟦1:167⟧
And from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
Sālim, client (المولى) of Abū Ḥudhayfah, used to lead in prayer the Emigrants who came from Mecca when they arrived in Medina, because he was the best of them in reciting (1) .
الواقدي: حدثنا أفلح بن سعيد، عن محمد بن كعب القرظي، قال:
Sālim used to lead the Emigrants in prayer at Qubāʾ, ʿUmar being among them, before the Messenger of Allah (2) ﷺ arrived.
حنظلة بن أبي سفيان: عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط، عن عائشة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah found me late one night and said: (What kept you?) .
I said: In the mosque there is the most beautiful voice I have heard reciting the Qurʾān.
He took his cloak and went out to listen to him, and it was Sālim, client (المولى) of Abū Ḥudhayfah.
He said: (Praise be to Allah who has placed in my community the like of you (3)) .
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is good.
عبد الله بن نمير: عن عبيد الله، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر:
That the Emigrants stopped at al-ʿUṣbah beside Qubāʾ, and Sālim, client (المولى) of Abū Ḥudhayfah, led them in prayer, because he was ⟦1:168⟧ the one among them with the most Qurʾān, and among them were ʿUmar and Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad (1) .
Usāmah ibn Ḥafṣ narrated it from ʿUbayd Allāh, and his wording:
When the first Emigrants arrived at al-ʿUṣbah before the arrival of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Sālim used to lead them in prayer.
It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, who said:
The Prophet ﷺ paired Sālim, client (المولى) of Abū Ḥudhayfah, in brotherhood with Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.
This is disconnected.
And there came in the narration of al-Wāqidī: that Muḥammad ibn Thābit ibn Qays said:
When the Muslims were routed on the day of al-Yamāmah, Sālim, client (المولى) of Abū Ḥudhayfah, said: This is not how we used to do with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He dug a pit for himself and stood in it, carrying the banner of the Emigrants that day, then fought until he was killed (2) .
ʿUbayd ibn Abī al-Jaʿd narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Hād:
That Sālim sold his inheritance to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and it reached 200 dirhams, so he gave it to his mother and said: Eat it.
It is said: Sālim and his client (المولى) Abū Ḥudhayfah were found, the head of one beside the feet of the other, both fallen - (may Allah be pleased with both of them) (3) -.
Among the virtues of Sālim: ⟦1:169⟧
أخبرنا الإمام أبو محمد عبد الرحمن بن محمد في كتابه، وجماعة، قالوا:
أخبرنا حنبل بن عبد الله، أنبأنا هبة الله بن محمد، أنبأنا أبو علي بن المذهب، أنبأنا أحمد بن جعفر، حدثنا عبد الله بن أحمد، حدثني أبي، حدثنا عفان، حدثنا حماد، عن علي بن زيد، عن أبي رافع:
That ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: Whoever of the captives of the Arabs reaches my death, he is from the property of Allah.
Saʿīd ibn Zayd said: If you were to point to a man from among the Muslims, the people would trust you; Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq did that and the people trusted him.
He said: I have seen from my companions a bad eagerness, and I am entrusting this matter to these six men.
Then he said: If either of two men had reached me, and I had then entrusted the matter to him, I would have trusted him: Sālim, client (المولى) of Abū Ḥudhayfah, and Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (1) .
ʿAlī ibn Zayd: soft in hadith (لين الحديث) (2) . If this is correct, it indicates the stature of these two in the heart of ʿUmar, and that the imamate is permissible in other than a Qurashī, and Allah knows best.
